name: Improve eye contact
blurb: Comfortable, natural eye contact — not staring — changes how people read your confidence and warmth. It responds quickly to deliberate practice.
steps: Learn the target: roughly 50% while speaking and 70% while listening, in comfortable stretches broken by natural glances away.
Practise the triangle technique: move your gaze slowly between their two eyes and mouth, which reads as engaged rather than fixed.
Break contact sideways rather than downwards. Looking down reads as submission or dishonesty.
Start with low-stakes practice: baristas, shopkeepers, colleagues you pass.
Notice the discomfort threshold and extend it by a second at a time.
Watch a good interviewer and study when they hold and when they release.
tips: Unbroken staring is worse than too little. The pattern of breaks is what makes it comfortable.
Eye-contact norms vary a lot between cultures. Calibrate to context rather than applying one rule everywhere.
proof: You hold comfortable eye contact through a whole conversation without either party feeling scrutinised.
